title: ONI Companion Link: live.json (schema 1 and 2, v1.3 additions)
description: FROZEN after P1 (v1.1). Schema 2 only adds fields: the core reads both 1 and 2. Written by the mod to <ONI user folder>/companion/live/live.json via write-tmp-then-rename. Written only when something changed, at most once per real second while unpaused, at once on pause / cycle change / new alert / save. When the colony unloads it writes state "menu". When state is "running" the fields listed under `if/then` are required. Units: mass kg, temperature Celsius, time seconds unless named otherwise.

schema.description: 2 = v1.1 mod: dupe appearanceHash, statusItems, diseases, stamina, bodyTempC, attributes; resources as a categorized list.

seq.description: Increases by 1 on every write within one game session; may restart at 1 in a new session (the core also compares writtenAt).

state.description: menu: the game is at its main menu (rewritten every 60 s by mod 0.4.1+). stopped: the game quit (mod 0.4.1+; a crash writes nothing, readers go by writtenAt).

dlcIds.description: Active DLC ids (game ids). Empty = base game.

cycle.description: Current cycle number, as the game shows it (starts at 1).

timeOfDay.description: Fraction of the 600 s cycle that has elapsed.

speed.description: Game speed setting; keeps its value while paused.

activeWorldId.description: World the player is looking at; matches worlds[].id.

contract.description: v1.3. Contract level the mod was built for (3 = v1.3). Absent = a mod before v1.3.

requiresCore.description: v1.3. The core versions this mod works with (inclusive dotted numbers; no max = no upper limit).

activeOverlay.description: v1.3. The game's active overlay mode id (an export overlays[].id); null = no overlay. Written at once when it changes, also when the player changes it in the game.

activeTool.description: v1.3. The game's active tool id (an export tools[].id); null = no tool (the normal select state). Written at once on change.

priority.description: v1.3. The game's current priority setting for the next tool: 1..9, or the string "emergency". Written at once on change.

unlockedBuildings.description: v1.3. Ids of the buildings the game lets the player build now (its own rule: researched or free). Rewritten when research finishes.

writeMs.description: Main-thread time of this write, for the 2 ms budget.

id.description: Stable per duplicant within a colony. Schema 2: the game's instance id as a decimal string; it is what commands target ({kind:"dupe", id}).

appearanceHash.description: Schema 2. Changes when hair, face, outfit or hat changes; names the portrait file.

chore.description: Current task, display text from the game; null when idle.

statusItems.description: Schema 2. The duplicant's active status items, the game's own. The core builds warning badges from these.

attributes.description: Schema 2. Skill attributes (Athletics, Digging, ...), the game's own names.

severity.description: The game's own notification type for this status item.

ResourceItem.description: Schema 2. One row of the game's Resources panel for one world, in the game's own category and item order.

id.description: Resource tag or element id (same ids as the schema 1 map).

category.description: The game's category name (Metal, Food, Liquids, ...). The list order is the game's order; the core never re-sorts categories.

kcal.description: Food only: energy per unit, when known.

id.description: Critter prefab id (matches a critter entry id).

tame.description: How many of count are tame.

title.description: v1.2. The game's notification title, as shown in the alert list (may carry TextMeshPro markup like tooltipMarkup). `text` stays the plain-text form.

type.description: v1.2. The game's own NotificationType, camelCased, written as the mod found it by decompiling (expected: bad, minorBad, neutral, good, event, messages, messageImportant, custom, tutorial, duplicantThreatening). `level` is the coarse mapping the v1.1 core already understands. The core never hard-codes behavior per type; it only picks a tone and an icon from it.

tooltipMarkup.description: v1.2. The exact string the game's tooltip builds for this alert, with its TextMeshPro markup (<b>, <color>, <link>, <sprite>, line breaks). Built by the mod only when the set of alerts changes. The core turns it into spans. The mod wraps each distinct source line (the game's bullet-name lines) in <link="N">...</link> (N = links[].index); the game itself has no per-line links.

links.description: v1.2. One per highlighted (<link>) line of the tooltip, in order. `index` is what alert_activate {link} sends.

click.description: v1.2. The main click result, read from the game's own notification object.

dismissable.description: v1.2. True only when the game itself lets the player dismiss this alert. Absent = false.

AlertLink.description: v1.2. One highlighted line of an alert tooltip and what a click on it does in the game.

index.description: Position among the alert's links (0-based); the <link> id in tooltipMarkup is the same number.

label.description: Plain text of the highlighted line.

kind.description: focus = the game moves the camera to a target (cycling like the game); screen = the game opens a screen.

target.description: focus: display name of the thing the camera moves to; screen: a screen id from the list in AlertClick. Informational: the mod resolves the real target itself from the alert.

AlertClick.description: v1.2. What clicking the alert itself does in the game.

target.description: kind screen: one of research, skills, schedule, consumables, report, codex, starmap, vitals, jobs, resources, diagnostics, message (a message alert opens the game's message dialog), other (a custom callback that is not a management screen). The game's Codex toggle is reported as codex and its Jobs toggle as jobs; database and priorities are never emitted. Absent for focus (the mod picks the target) and none.

queue.description: In order, current first when there is one.

resources.description: Schema 1: object, resource tag or element id -> kg available in this world. Schema 2: list of ResourceItem. The core accepts both.

stock.description: v1.3. Element id -> kg available in this world for building, from the same inventory the game's material picker uses. Only elements that are a candidate for some building material slot (export materials[].candidates). Absent = not known.

power.description: Omit when not cheap to gather.
